utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-02-58-I, the Prosecutor versus Ljubisa Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, good morning, everyone. We're here on account of the amendment of the indictment to include new charges, thus giving rise to the need for a further initial appearance in terms of Rule 50 of the Rules of Procedure. First of all, would the parties' representatives identify themselves, please. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning Your Honour, may it please the court, it's Antoinette Issa on behalf of the Prosecution and with me is Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. John Ostojic on behalf of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic. Now, Mr. Ostojic, the accused would be entitled to insist on a reading, a fresh reading of the indictment in this case if he wished. Does he wish to do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: After consulting with him, Your Honour, he does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Beara, could you stand, please. As I said a moment ago, we are here because of the amendment of the indictment giving rise to the need for a further appearance so that you can tender pleas in respect of what I consider to be new charges arising out of the amendment to the indictment. You will recollect that previously you were charged under counts 1(A) and (B) in the alternative with genocide or alternative complicity in genocide. The second of these, complicity in genocide, has been removed from the indictment and in its place there is a new Count 2 charging you with conspiracy to commit genocide. So that is the first significant amendment, and that gives rise to the need to tender a plea in respect of Count 2 afresh. The other changes to the indictment that give rise to this situation are that you are now implicated, allegedly, in forceable transfers as part of your involvement in a joint criminal enterprise. In other words, you're charged with the commission of forcible transfers as the result of your involvement in a joint criminal enterprise, and that enterprise is now described as including forcible transfer. That again, in my view, gave rise to new charges, and that means that you will be required to tender pleas afresh in respect of counts 6 and 7. Now, what will now happen is that the Registrar will read to you in brief form the specific terms of Count 2, and she will then ask you whether you plead guilty or not guilty, and you will answer that question. She will then do the same exercise in respect of Counts 6 and 7. As far as Count 2 is concerned, if I can just give you that example, she will simply say to you that you are charged under Count 2 with conspiracy to commit genocide punishable under Articles 4(3)(b) and 7(1) of the statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead to that charge, guilty or not guilty, and you will then answer the question. Now, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you now take the pleas.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Beara, you are charged conspiracy to commit genocide punishable under Articles 4(3)(b) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: You are charged with Count 6, persecution --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Pause please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on a second. There was no translation of that plea because of the microphone. Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, just for the avoidance of doubt, the transcript shows you're charged with Count 6. In fact, this is Count 2 that we are dealing with. I don't think the word 6 was actually used. There was no reference to the count number at all so I think for the avoidance of any doubt we'll go through that exercise again. In fact it might be better if I deal with this. If you just sit down for the moment it might be easier if I deal with this. Mr. Beara, you're charged under Count 2 with conspiracy to commit genocide, punishable under Articles 4(3)(b) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead to that charge, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. You are charged under Count 6 with persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, including murder, cruel and inhumane treatment, terrorising the civilian population, destruction of personal property, and forcible transfer punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead do that count, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And then lastly you're charged under Count 7 with inhumane acts, forcible transfer a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead to that count, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. You may now sit. Thank you. Now, as a result of these pleas combined with the pleas of not guilty previously tendered by Mr. Beara, the Registrar will take note that a trial must be fixed in due course. Mr. Ostojic, as already indicated in earlier order of the Chamber, the period for preliminary motions, period of 30 days that is revived as a result of this process, is already running and is running from the 30th of March, I think, in terms of that order. So I take it that it has been drawn to Mr. Beara's attention that if he has any preliminary motions to make then he has until about the end of this month to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I knows also that there is a Status Conference in this case on the 15th of June, and that Status Conference will stand. It should take place on that occasion. Can you clarify, just confirm for me that as far as you are concerned, as far as you're aware, all disclosure has been made in appropriate form.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I did receive this morning, Your Honour, some documents that are signature on the Defence counsel desk. To the extent that I haven't had a chance to review this, I believe that they are complying in part, and I don't think we have an issue or a problem with the Prosecution at this time with the compliance of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Right. And is there any other matter that Mr. Beara would wish to raise with the Court at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not at this time, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, are there any matters that the Prosecution would wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you clarify just the one thing for me about disclosure. On the assumption that the disclosure was complete, the order that was issued indicated the 30-day period was running from the 30th of March. Does the bundle on the Defence table indicate that the situation should have been otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I can indicate, Your Honour, that we obviously started to make disclosure before today. We actually did provide some disclosure on the last occasion. We also provided disclosure under 66(A)(i) which is now complete and we are continuing to provide disclosure. As Your Honour may be aware, there are a number of accused that are now present in the Tribunal that are related to the Srebrenica case. We may have indicated on a prior occasion that we are -- we may be bringing a joinder application to join the -- these accused, and consequently we're looking at the disclosure from a global perspective in terms of all the accused and we do intend to provide disclosure on the electronic database system in an efficient manner, taking into account all the accused that are present before the -- in the Tribunal currently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. So just one other point, Ms. Issa. The disclosure in terms of 66(A)(i), that's the supporting material and the prior statements of the accused, was that so far as the amended indictment is concerned completed prior to the 30th of March?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it has been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the order that was made earlier is in an appropriate form and that the 30 days for preliminary motions would start running on the 30th of March, the day that the fresh indictment was filed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that completes the matters that require to be dealt with this morning. The Court is accordingly adjourned.
